name: Capture
summary: How memory gets written: taste signals and evidence, automatic session capture, note markers, inbox capture and session summaries.

features.name: Feedback signals and evidence
features.summary: Agents record taste signals, applied or violated evidence and log milestones; reminders keep them doing it.
capabilities: Writes each taste signal (topic, sign, principle, scope or `feedback.default_scope`) to the inbox or the store
With `force_confirmed`, adds a confirmed rule that skips the dream trial, when a permissions document allows it
Logs applied, violated or outdated evidence against a rule; an outdated event retires the rule
Appends one-line narrative notes (a release, a merge, a finding) to the day log (`brain_note`)
Imports another tool's memory files as unconfirmed rules through a format adapter: a dry run, then a digest-bound apply
Commits an agent's derived conclusion as an unconfirmed rule that cites its premise rules (`brain_derive_fact`)
Packs and unpacks session prose losslessly, keeping structured content byte for byte (`brain codec`)
Reminds the agent after each file edit, and at Stop when the turn's edits logged no brain event (on by default)
limits: Signals and evidence change no rule until the dream pass runs; only force_confirmed writes a rule at once.
The CLI brain feedback skips the principle quality gate that the MCP tool and session replays apply.
The reminder hooks count only Write, Edit, MultiEdit and apply_patch calls as artifacts.

features.name: Automatic session capture
features.summary: Lifecycle hooks turn prompt markers, facts and brain_feedback calls into signals and log session events.
capabilities: Runs on session start and end, each prompt, brain_feedback calls, Stop, SubagentStop and PostCompact.
Turns @osb feedback markers in prompts and successful brain_feedback inputs into signals, deduped by hash.
Extracts URLs, e-mail addresses and currency or percent amounts from user prompts as facts, no model call.
Applies the sessions block first: ignore and stateless session globs, ignore_message_patterns regexes.
Defers dedup-heavy events to a detached per-vault worker; OPEN_SECOND_BRAIN_SESSION_CAPTURE_DEFER=0 stops it.
Re-reads the transcript's user turns when a SessionEnd reports an interrupted session
Logs a lifecycle row and an audit record with counters per event, also from stdin (`brain session-hook`)
An async Claude Code Stop hook passes queued end-of-turn advisories to the model with the next prompt.
limits: Reads user turns only; assistant output is never captured as a marker or a fact.
Records nothing for a dream session, and only the audit row for an ignored session.
Failures exit 0 silently; a ceiling timeout is recorded only in the hook audit log.

features.name: Inline note markers
features.summary: @osb markers and inline citations in notes become captured items, dated events or front matter write-backs.
capabilities: Parses @osb markers as a start-of-line form or an osb fenced YAML block; other code fences are skipped.
scan-inline turns feedback markers into inbox signals, deduped by hash, and marks each @osb✓ [[sig-id]].
Routes fact markers through premise checks to unconfirmed rules and skill markers to pending proposals.
Scans notes.read_paths or --path roots only, skips Brain/ and vault.ignore_paths, reports files over 1 MiB.
apply-markers reports @osb set note= field= value= writes; --apply needs guardrails.marker_writeback.
Validates each set value against the schema pack, logs an attribute-write event, leaves bad targets live.
scan-citations makes [Source: <name>, YYYY-MM-DD] dated source-citation timeline events, deduped by name+date.
Previews scan-inline and scan-citations without writing (`--dry-run`)
limits: Runs only when a CLI verb is invoked; no hook or MCP tool scans notes for markers.
scan-inline scans nothing when notes.read_paths is empty and no --path is given.
Citation dates must be ISO YYYY-MM-DD; other date forms are reported as malformed.
Loop markers are never consumed here; they are read live by the today view.

features.name: Inbox capture
features.summary: Stages captures from the terminal or a Telegram bot and routes them to sources, notes or obligations.
capabilities: brain capture stages text from an argument or stdin as a cap-<date>-<time>-<hash> page under Brain/captures/.
Stamps each capture with its source channel, sender and time
telegram-capture run long-polls getUpdates (30 s) and stages each text message from an allowlisted chat id.
Logs each rejected, malformed or refused Telegram update as a decision; API errors back off 1 s up to 30 s.
Replies to `/catchup` with the captures since the last acknowledged one
inbox-drain sends a lone URL to source ingest and a leading @obligation to an obligation (default weekly).
Routes every other capture to a create-or-merge idea note in captured/ and archives it to processed/.
Plans the routes as a dry run until `inbox-drain --apply`
limits: The Telegram bot runs only while telegram-capture run is in the foreground; no hook or daemon starts it.
An empty telegram_chat_allowlist (the default) accepts no chat; a missing bot token is a startup error.
Classification uses structure only (URL shape, @obligation token), never the wording of the text.

features.name: Session summaries and handoffs
features.summary: Stores a structured session digest of decisions, learnings and next steps, and writes handoff notes.
capabilities: Stores an agent-written digest (request, decisions, learnings, next steps) as an append-only record.
Dedups a digest by a sha256 of its content per session and project_scope; an all-empty digest is refused.
Returns a session's latest digest with its digest count, flagging divergent ones (`get`)
Lists digests filtered by session id or project scope
brain_session_checkpoint saves signals, a digest and a diary log line in one call keyed by the session id.
A checkpoint retry with equal content is a no-op, other content a mismatch error; failed items return partial.
brain handoff writes Brain/handoffs/<date>-<scope>.md (request, done, files, learned, next) from a transcript.
SessionEnd writes the handoff note itself when session_handoff is true (default off).
limits: The digest categories come from the agent; the kernel never extracts them from prose.
Handoff sections are filled by English keyword regexes, at most 5 lines each.
Handoff reads only transcripts of the registered adapters: claude, codex, hermes, opencode and grok.
Divergent digests are reported, never merged or reconciled.
